messages:
kevin: Heads up — we've got ~8 pods Pending with `0/4 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` but the cluster metrics show ~6 free GPUs in other nodepools. Autoscaler didn't react. Anyone else seeing this?
ops-bot: Cluster Autoscaler event: "Scale-up skipped: no node groups left under max size" (nodegroup: gpu-training-us-west).
maya: can you paste `kubectl describe` for one of the pending pods? also which nodeSelector/affinity the pod uses?
kevin: pasted below:
```
Name:           model-train-rtx-fallback-7
Namespace:      ml-training
Node-Selector:  pool: training
Tolerations:    <none>
Containers:
  trainer:
    Requests:  nvidia.com/gpu: 2
Events:
  00:12:33  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x20 over 7m)  default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 4 node(s) didn't match node selector.
```
kevin: note the cluster has another nodepool (gpu-burst) with 6 free GPUs but its nodes are labeled `pool: burst` and `gpu-family: rtx-a6000` while training pool is `gpu-family: a100`. Pods have no explicit gpu-family requirement, but nodeSelector is `pool: training` because of legacy deploys.
sanjay: sounds like two issues: (1) nodeSelector is forcing them into the training pool which is at max and CA can't scale it further, (2) fragmentation: each training node has 1 free GPU but pod needs 2 so scheduler can't pack. the free GPUs in burst pool are irrelevant because of nodeSelector.
nina: also check nodegroup autoscaling limits — training pool hit its max size this morning after the nightly batch. CA logs show `max size reached` for that group.
kevin: confirmed: training pool size == 12 (max). burst pool has headroom but different label.
maya: two quick mitigation options: (A) relax the nodeSelector/podAffinity so scheduler can use `pool: burst` temporarily, or (B) create a short-lived nodegroup increase for training pool and scale manually.
sanjay: longer-term: we should make the scheduler fallback-aware. options: add a `gpu-fallback` nodeSelector logic in the deployment (priority class + soft nodeAffinity) or implement smart routing in the service that can choose quantized model variants for cheaper GPUs.
kevin: cost note — if we start sending training jobs to burst (rtx-a6000) we may see 15-25% slower throughput for this model; cheaper than spinning more a100s but affects SLA.
maya: for immediate unblock I've applied a patch to the deployment that changes `nodeSelector: pool: training` -> `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` with `pool: burst` as second preference. rolling it now.
deploy-bot: Deployment model-train-rtx-fallback updated: 3->3 rolling update started.
kevin: after the patch 4 pods scheduled onto burst pool, 2 still Pending because they need 2 GPUs and nodes there only have 1 free each. fragmentation still an issue.
sanjay: we can try two more temp steps: (1) binpack smaller jobs by setting `topologySpreadConstraints` to prefer same-node placement and setting `requests.gpu` appropriately, (2) temporarily cordon a few training nodes so CA will add capacity to burst pool (works because burst pool has lower utilization).
nina: I'll open a short ticket to bump training pool max by 3 for 2 hours to clear backlog, then revert. include cost estimate.
kevin: action items: @nina raise temp quota, @sanjay make a small scheduler fallback doc (how to prefer burst pool), @maya monitor latencies and rollback if >10% regression. thanks all :thumbsup:
